findings.where: Article page specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in logo blue. The tile's own palette gives blue only three jobs: the wordmark, links and the button. Here it is used for decoration as well. So in an article the same blue now means both 'you can act on this' and 'a quote', and a large blue italic line pulls the eye more strongly than the one real link below it.
findings.who_objects: A reader at a development bank skimming one of Mark's articles, who could take the blue line for a link or a heading to click. Angélique would object too: every pull quote she adds to a post would spread the action colour through the article, and blue would lose its meaning as the thing to act on. That meaning is the 'Get in touch' button's.

findings.where: Style tile section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' each have a hairline rule under the label, but 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' do not (desktop-02, phone-01, phone-02)
findings.fault: Section labels of the same kind are treated differently. Two of the five have a divider and three do not, and nothing in the content explains the difference. So the tile does not settle whether a section heading takes a rule.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Mark reading the tile as the look, and the layout round building from it. Both need to know whether a hairline under a section heading is part of the house treatment, and the tile gives both answers.
